theorem p10_factorial_pow :
    IsGreatest {n : ℕ | Nat.factorial n < 3 ^ n} p10_answer := by
  constructor
  · -- Show 6 is in the set: 6! < 3^6
    norm_num [Nat.factorial]
  · -- Show 6 is an upper bound: for all n > 6, n! ≥ 3^n
    intro n hn
    by_contra h
    -- If n ∈ S and n ≠ 6, then n > 6 (since 6 ∈ S)

      omega
    -- Prove by induction that for all k ≥ 7, k! ≥ 3^k

      intro k hk
      induction' hk with k hk IH
      · -- Base case: k = 7
        norm_num [Nat.factorial]
      · -- Inductive step: assume k! ≥ 3^k, prove (k+1)! ≥ 3^(k+1)
        simp [Nat.factorial, pow_succ] at *
        have h₃ : k + 1 ≥ 8 := by omega
        have h₄ : (k + 1 : ℕ) ≥ 3 := by omega
        nlinarith
    -- Apply the lemma to n
    have h₃ : Nat.factorial n ≥ 3 ^ n := h₂ n h₁
    -- This contradicts hn: n! < 3^n
